title: Spinless charged excitation at the interface between a conventional topological insulator and a topological Mott insulator
authors: Cesar A. Gallegos, Andrew J. Millis, Steven R. White
abstract: We investigate the interface separating two topologically distinct insulating phases of matter using extensive density-matrix renormalization group calculations to study the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model with a spatially varying interaction strength, chosen to realize both integer quantum Hall and chiral spin liquid states in different spatial regions. We find that the integer quantum Hall-chiral spin liquid interface hosts a spinless charged excitation that is bound to the interface. This mode at the interface is identified through charge and spin pumping, and by direct calculations of low-lying excited states. We also characterize bulk excitations in both phases, finding evidence for fractionalization in the chiral spin liquid and for spin-triplet exciton formation in the integer quantum Hall phase.
summary: This theoretical work uses DMRG on the Hofstadter-Hubbard model to examine an interface between a Quantum Hall insulator and a Chiral Spin Liquid. The primary finding is the existence of a gapless, spinless charged excitation localized at this boundary. The research also details how bulk excitations in both phases exhibit characteristic signatures of fractionalization or electron-hole binding.
main_problem: The study investigates exotic excitations at the interface separating two distinct topological insulating phases: an Integer Quantum Hall (IQH) phase and a Chiral Spin Liquid (CSL) phase.
main_result: The IQH–CSL interface hosts a unique, gapless spinless charged excitation. Furthermore, bulk analysis reveals fractionalization in the CSL phase and exciton formation in the IQH phase.
method: Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations were extensively used to study both topological response to fluxes and low-lying excited states across the interface.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model, parameterized with spatially varying interaction strengths ($U$) to realize the IQH (TI) and CSL (TMI) regimes.
key_observables: Charge density deviation ($	ext{n} - 	ext{n}_{	ext{gs}}$), local magnetization ($S_z$), charge/spin pumping, and binding energies of spin-triplet excitons.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the half-filled ground state regime, comparing regimes with $U=8$ (IQH) and $U=14$ (CSL).
main_assumptions: The calculations are performed on finite-radius cylinders (YC3, YC5), and results rely on DMRG sweeps which serve as diagnostics for identifying characteristic fractionalized structures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate charge/spin density profiles under flux insertion, compare single-particle excitations in bulk IQH vs CSL phases, and track the energy evolution of two-particle states across different bond dimensions ($\chi$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the interface by first characterizing bulk excitations (fractionalization in CSL, excitons in IQH), then using pumping measurements to identify the gapless edge mode, and finally analyzing two-particle excited states to confirm spinon/chargon separation at the boundary.
why_interesting: The study of topological interfaces and fractionalized excitations is highly relevant to understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems, which often exhibit complex quantum ground states beyond simple band theory predictions.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Magnetic unit cell of the triangular lattice with flux π/2 per triangle. Nonzero Peierls hopping phases are shown. (b) Representative IQH–CSL YC6 cylinder under flux insertion Φ. Change in position dependent charge den- sity nΦ −nΦ=0 (c) and spin density Sz Φ −Sz Φ=0 (d) caused by threading the same and opposite fluxes for the two spin species, respectively, in 40 × 6 cylinders. The charge and spin pumped for different fluxes are shifted by 0.1 for clarity. The vertical red line in (b)-(d) indicates the IQH–CSL interface, and the orange large arrows indicate the pumping progres- sion.

FIG. 2. Single-particle bulk excitations in the [(a), (b)] IQH and [(c), (d)] CSL phases at U =8 and U =14, respectively, in a 240×3 cylinder keeping a bond dimension χ=800. The solid blue and purple lines show the deviation of the charge density from the ground state, n −ngs, and the local magnetization, Sz, respectively, for different sweeps. The electron-like exci- tation in the IQH and its spin-charge separation into a spinon and chargon in the CSL phase are indicated.

FIG. 4. (a) A separated electron-hole pair in the IQH phase at U =8 in a 240×3 cylinder. The solid blue and purple lines show the deviation of the charge density from the ground state, n−ngs, and the local magnetization, Sz, respectively. (b) The spin-triplet electron-hole binding energy from Eq. (2) as a function of U in the IQH phase. The blue dashed line indicates the IQH–CSL transition point Uc.

FIG. 3. Same as Fig. 2, but for the charge-neutral spin-triplet bulk excitation. The spin-triplet exciton in the IQH phase and the fractionalization into two spatially separated spinons in the CSL phase are indicated.

FIG. 5. Excited states at the IQH–CSL interface. The [(a), (c)] single-particle and [(b), (d)] charge-neutral spin-triplet excitation for [(a), (b)] YC3 (length 240) and [(c), (d)] YC5 (length 80) cylinders. The solid red line marks the IQH–CSL interface. The solid blue and purple lines show the deviation of the charge density from the ground state, n−ngs, and the local magnetization, Sz, respectively. The spinless charged excitations, chargon and holon, and the fractionalized spin excitation, spinon, are indicated.
